predecessors.name: Holy Roman Empire
predecessors.text: the county palatine of the Rhine, which the page dates 'From about 1085/86, after the death of the last Ezzonian count palatine'

successors.name: Duchy of Bavaria
successors.text: the Palatinate lands (Lower Palatinate around Heidelberg and Mannheim, Neuburg and Sulzbach) when 'Charles Theodore ... inherited the Electorate of Bavaria in 1777'; infobox 'Subsumed by Bavaria: 30…

ledger.x: 1085: the county palatine of the Rhine begins.
About 1182: Conrad moves the residence from Stahleck Castle near Bacharach to Heidelberg.
1214: the Palatinate passes to the Wittelsbachs.
1329: the Treaty of Pavia gives the Palatine line the Upper Palatinate.
10 January 1356: the Golden Bull makes the Palatinate an electorate.
October 1463: the Palatinate takes the Bergstrasse.
1559: the electorate passes to Frederick III of Simmern.
1621: Spanish troops hold the west of the Palatinate.
19 September 1622: Heidelberg falls to the Catholic army.
1623: the Bergstrasse pledge ends and Heppenheim is Mainz's again.
February 1623: Maximilian of Bavaria takes the Upper Palatinate and the electoral vote.
24 October 1648: the Lower Palatinate returns to the Elector Palatine.
September 1688: Louis XIV invades the Palatinate.
1690: Johann Wilhelm moves the residence from Heidelberg to Düsseldorf (infobox 'Düsseldorf; (1690-1720)').
1697: the Peace of Ryswick ends the fighting.
30 December 1777: the Palatinate passes to Bavaria.

wars.name: Palatinate campaign
wars.outcome: Catholic victory: the Palatinate is occupied, Frederick V is removed as elector in February 1623 and the Upper Palatinate goes to Bavaria; the Spanish stay in the west until 1652.

wars.name: Nine Years' War
wars.outcome: France invades in September 1688, burns Heidelberg and Mannheim in March 1689 and raids again in 1693; by the 1697 Peace of Ryswick France gives up 'gains on the right bank of the Rhine' and its Palatinate claim.

certainty.note: The pages give towns and lines of succession, no boundaries; the Palatinate is a patchwork of scattered lands.
The Peace of Westphalia (1648) fixed the Lower Palatinate and left the Upper Palatinate with Bavaria; enclave and cadet-line frontiers inside the state remain approximate.
